data.turoyo: Kməbʕəǧ darḥal. Awwəl d kmoṭe, kmoḥe u reḥo b qarʕe, kmagəžle, kməbʕəǧ, ḥaša, bayn i pisiye.
data.translation: He suffocates immediately. As soon as he arrives, the smell hits his head, makes him dizzy; he suffocates, with pardon, among the filth.

data.translation: <...> Ich schoß auf sie, doch die Kugel traf sie nicht. Da fiel siebewußtlos nieder, und ich fing sie. Sie ist ganz unverletzt. <...>

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive/1; third-person feminine change of state in a complete context, distinct from the inherited first-person quotation.

data.turoyo: E umarno: "Bu bayto lə ḥzeli ḥa mənayxu, d aṯi li ʕito w lo d mṣalele, magəžxullan bu gəmgəmano dəṯxu!... Kula mi zəʕṯo yo! Aloho ġalabe lə kmaqbela!"
data.translation: Yes, I say, “At home I never saw one of you come to church or pray, and you have driven us crazy with this mumbling of yours!... It is all from fear! God does not accept it very much!”

rationale: III Preterit 1 has two inherited examples; 2pl agent plus 1pl affected object and b-cause adds a clear interpersonal aggravation context.

summary: Hors 2/88 and 2/95 present the same shooting episode from different viewpoints. The first-person feminine form is already cited as MM 88; only the distinct third-person feminine context is added to the thin Preterit Intransitive cell.

The absence of a bullet impact is explicit (lo qayəṯ eba), followed by gayižo and falling. This supports becoming stunned within I.1; it does not require a separate fainting sense inferred from German.

III Magəžluxlan has second-person L-agent and first-plural affected object. The verbal causative is already listed and the 73/110 occurrence already quoted; the Kurdish etymology does not make this a light verb plus noun collocation.
Infectum kmagəžle has a k-prefix and a patient suffix; its -le is not a Preterit l-agent merely because the ending is homographic.
The cause phrase bu gəmgəmano contrasts with smell as grammatical cause subject. No experiencer-subject or Detransitive construction occurs.
Round-1 stunned/fainting evidence and citation questions remain baseline, with no repeated proposal.

The German at Hors 2/95 combines gayižo with the following Nafilo as 'Da fiel siebewußtlos nieder'. Keep the combined clause and confirm any finer distinction between being stunned, fainting and dizziness with a speaker.
Confirm how Hors 2 and inherited MM references correspond before altering the MM 88 citation.

Can speakers delimit bodily dizziness from being mentally overwhelmed within the existing German gloss? Jan’s two causal contexts support the inherited broad range but do not establish a new boundary.
Inanimate smell causes bodily dizziness, while companions’ mumbling causes aggravation. Both fit the inherited causative range without a new numbered sense.
